name: Google Drive
alternative: drive.file scope with the Google Picker (only files the person picks, non-sensitive, no audit), or the Google Drive for desktop synced folder on the Mac
notes: Google runs a remote Drive MCP (Workspace Developer Preview) that needs a pre-registered Google Cloud OAuth client and the restricted drive.readonly scope, so full Drive access needs restricted-scope verification and a security assessment at least every 12 months; whether the preview admits personal Gmail accounts is not stated. Discovery 2026-10-08: protected-resource metadata only at the path-suffixed URL, authorization server accounts.google.com, DCR no, CIMD no, S256 (also plain).

name: Affirm
alternative: Affirm statement and payment emails in the person's mailbox, or the PDF statements they download from their Affirm account
notes: Affirm's API is for merchant developers integrating checkout; there is no consumer account API and no Affirm MCP in the MCP Registry (only unrelated names). Discovery 2026-10-08: no MCP or OAuth metadata found. Aggregators such as Plaid exist but route data through a third party; excluded.

name: Chess.com
alternative: none
notes: The read-only Published-Data API (api.chess.com/pub) needs no key and covers the person's public profile, stats and monthly game archives; private data (game chat, conditional moves) needs an OAuth app granted through Chess.com's application form (review). No vendor MCP; community servers include github.com/pab1it0/chess-mcp. Discovery 2026-10-08: no MCP or OAuth metadata found.

name: Google Search
alternative: The person's Google Takeout export of My Activity (Search history)
notes: There is no API to a person's Search account or history, and the Custom Search JSON API is closed to new customers and ends for existing ones on 2027-01-01. Google's official remote MCP servers in the registry (com.googleapis.*) cover Cloud and Maps, not web Search; Search-named entries are community or third-party SERP services. Grounding with Google Search in the paid Gemini API is a model feature, not account access.

name: GroupMe
alternative: none
notes: GroupMe's public v3 API (groups, messages, direct messages) accepts the access token the person copies from dev.groupme.com (needs a password login, not single sign-on), or a token from a free client ID registered once with no documented review; the token grants full account access. No MCP in the MCP Registry. Discovery 2026-10-08: no MCP or OAuth metadata found.

name: Crunchyroll
alternative: A privacy access request for a portable copy of the person's account data (one-off, not a live connection)
notes: Crunchyroll publishes no developer API; watchlist and history are only in its apps. The community server github.com/markswendsen-code/mcp-crunchyroll drives the private web API and is not affiliated. Discovery 2026-10-08: no MCP or OAuth metadata found.

name: WeightWatchers
alternative: Activity data the person keeps in Apple Health, which WW also reads, through an iOS Shortcut; the WW food and Points log has no export
notes: WeightWatchers has no public or developer API; its integrations (Apple Health, Fitbit, Withings) are partner syncs into the WW app, and the affiliate programme is marketing only. No MCP in the MCP Registry. Discovery 2026-10-08: no MCP or OAuth metadata found.

name: Domino's
alternative: Order confirmation emails in the person's mailbox
notes: Domino's offers ordering only through its own AnyWare channels (app, Alexa, Google, Slack, text, cars) and publishes no developer API. Community servers (e.g. the pizzamcp npm package) use the undocumented website API, which blocks cloud IPs and may hit CAPTCHAs. Discovery 2026-10-08: no MCP or OAuth metadata found.

name: Plex
alternative: none
notes: Plex publishes an official OpenAPI reference for Plex Media Server; an app picks its own name and client identifier (no registration or vetting), the person approves a PIN on plex.tv, and the app gets a 7-day JWT or legacy X-Plex-Token. No vendor MCP; community servers include github.com/niavasha/plex-mcp-server. Discovery 2026-10-08: no MCP or OAuth metadata found.

name: Gopuff
alternative: Order receipt emails ("Your Gopuff order!") in the person's mailbox
notes: Gopuff's only APIs are the Powered by Gopuff partner APIs for brands and retailers to fulfil their own orders, not usable on a shopper's account. No MCP in the MCP Registry. Discovery 2026-10-08: no MCP or OAuth metadata found.

name: Binance
alternative: Binance's public REST API with API keys the person creates
notes: Binance's official remote MCP (Agent OS) signs the person in on binance.com and trades only in a dedicated Agentic sub-account with no withdrawal scope; its docs list named clients, so acceptance of other CIMD clients is unverified. Discovery 2026-10-08: DCR no, CIMD yes, S256 (protected-resource metadata only at the root path; token auth none). Not in the MCP Registry under a Binance namespace.

name: Careem
alternative: Ride and order receipt emails in the person's mailbox (IMAP)
notes: No public consumer API or MCP found for Careem rides, food or pay; only the apps. No registry entry found.

name: OnePay
alternative: Statement export (PDF/CSV) and transaction alert emails
notes: OnePay (Walmart-backed fintech) publishes no consumer API or MCP; access is app only. No registry entry found.

name: MacroFactor
alternative: The person's in-app Data Export (Quick or Granular spreadsheet)
notes: No public API; the app offers Quick and Granular data export of nutrition, weight and workouts. Registry lists only community github.com/NasserAlbusaidi/macrofactor-mcp, which reads those exports; MacroFactor is a paid subscription.

name: Misfits Market
alternative: Order and delivery emails in the person's mailbox (IMAP)
notes: No public consumer API or MCP; ordering is through the website and app only. No registry entry found.

name: Chipotle
alternative: Order receipt and rewards emails in the person's mailbox (IMAP)
notes: No public ordering API. The registry entry is community github.com/markswendsen-code/mcp-chipotle (npm @striderlabs/mcp-chipotle), not Chipotle's own.

name: Greenlight
alternative: Monthly statements and transaction notification emails
notes: Greenlight (kids debit card) has no public consumer API or MCP. The registry hit greenlight (ai.agentlookups) is an unrelated solar-law server.

name: FEMA
alternative: none
notes: OpenFEMA is a free read-only public-data API with no key or registration; it covers public datasets (disasters, assistance, flood), not a person's DisasterAssistance.gov case. Registry entries are community (github.com/cyanheads/fema-mcp-server, com.olyport/fema, pipeworx gateways, which route through a third party).

name: Blinkist
alternative: Highlights and reading list shared by the person manually; Send-to-Kindle is for reading only
notes: No public API or MCP found; the app offers Send-to-Kindle but no documented export. Website blocks automated fetches, so this is based on the App Store listing.

name: Volvo Cars
alternative: The person creates and publishes their own Volvo developer API application and pastes its VCC API key and client credentials, as Home Assistant documents
notes: Volvo's Connected Vehicle and Energy APIs use Volvo ID OAuth plus a VCC API key per application; owner consent is required and full credentials for a shared app are granted manually (reported 14-21 days, developer portal blocked automated fetch). Volvo-ID logins expire weekly per evcc docs.

name: Xiaomi Home
alternative: Xiaomi devices exposed through Home Assistant's official Xiaomi Home integration, or Apple Home for HomeKit-capable devices
notes: No self-serve public cloud API; Xiaomi's own Home Assistant integration (github.com/XiaoMi/ha_xiaomi_home) signs in with Xiaomi's OAuth client to MIoT Cloud, with local control through a central hub gateway. MCP servers (e.g. github.com/oujiafan/mcp-mijia) are community and use unofficial APIs.

name: PDF Expert
alternative: Read and write the person's PDF files on the Mac directly; open files in PDF Expert through its URL scheme
notes: Readdle documents keyboard shortcuts and URL schemes for opening files but no API, AppleScript dictionary or MCP. Documents are ordinary local files, so Kipster can work on them without the app.
